summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individuals aged 70½ or older to exclude from their gross income certain direct charitable distributions made from employer-sponsored retirement plans, similar to existing rules for IRAs.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude certain charitable distributions from employer-sponsored retirement plans from gross income. This effectively lowers the taxable income for individuals making such distributions, thereby reducing tax revenue.

The bill creates a new tax exclusion allowing tax-free charitable distributions from employer-sponsored retirement plans (401(k)s, 403(b)s, 457 plans, SEPs, and SIMPLEs). This directly reduces federal tax revenue with no offsetting revenue raisers or spending cuts, increasing the deficit. The entire bill is devoted to enacting this revenue-reducing provision.
